line: Forty hand-embroidered cushion covers... needed in thirty days.
One AI shopping agent, ready to buy.
And the women who make them best sell only on WhatsApp... and none of them can make forty alone.
OpenStall Collective turns them into one supplier, in three steps: list, split, and pay on proof.
Claude does the talking. Code decides. PayPal holds the money.
Step one: list.
This is a real chat on OpenStall's WhatsApp number. A maker writes one line in Urdu... and sends a photo.
Claude reads the photo: a blue paisley cushion cover. Every number in the listing comes from the maker's own words.
OpenStall asks only for what's missing, one short question at a time, in Urdu.
One tap on haan, yes... and the stall is live, for any AI agent to read.
Step two: split.
A buyer's AI agent asks OpenStall's MCP storefront for forty covers, at most thirty dollars each.
Each maker's agent bids, and code checks every price against her floor and the buyer's maximum.
Plain code splits the order: twelve from Amina, eleven from Priya, ten from Lucía, seven from Grace... eight hundred and fifteen dollars.
The agent can't pay. A person approves one PayPal checkout, intent authorize... so PayPal only holds the money.
Each maker hears about her share on her phone, in her own language.
Step three: pay on proof.
Priya ships her parcel in Jaipur and photographs the courier receipt.
AI reads the courier and the tracking number... and Priya confirms with one tap.
Only then is her share captured from that one authorization, and paid out to her PayPal... with her tracking on the PayPal order.
In Pakistan, where Payouts can't reach, Amina is paid to her bank through Hyperwallet... simulated here, and labelled.
And if Grace can't make it?
Her share is released, never charged... and the other makers' agents bid for her seven covers, as a top-up.
Try to break it: ten real attacks... all refused by the code they target.
Every maker carries a signed trust passport. Change one number, and the signature fails.
Orders and payments run on APIMatic's PayPal SDK... and an ops agent checks them through PayPal's own MCP server, read-only.
A receipt photo can be faked, so next, the courier's own scan will release the money.
Claude talks.
Code decides.
PayPal pays on proof.
